newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bezeq raises $150 mln in syndicated loan.
newsitem.headline: Bezeq raises $150 mln in syndicated loan.

text.p: State-controlled Bezeq Israel Telecom has raised $150 million from a consortium of international banks, the company said in a statement on Tuesday.
The consortium was led by Switzerland's UBS, Germany's Dresdner Bank and Japan's Fuji Bank, the company said in a statement on Tuesday.

It said the loan was for seven years at Libor plus 0.325 percent and without guarantees. The proceeds will be used to finance the futher expansion of Bezeq's network, improved technology and new services.
The syndicate included five banks that had never before participated in a loan to Bezeq among them Citibank, which acted as a co-arranger.
Bezeq had sought a $100 million loan but the syndicate was oversubscribed. As a result, the company said, it opted to borrow a sum larger than planned for future financing needs.
The loan marks the fourth overseas syndicated borrowing by Bezeq, which is 76 percent-owned by the Israeli government and is the country's main telecommunications carrier.

Bezeq raised $150 million in October 1995, $200 million in March 1996 and another $150 million in October 1996, all for a period of five years. The last loan carried interest of Libor plus 0.3 percent.
